narrative.overview: The viewer is a recording from a logic analyzer. Every function is a decoded frame on a timeline, the line you stand on is a cursor, and the arrows on the block diagrams are signals that travel when you click.
keyCharacteristics: Timeline of decoded frames above the code, with a window that tracks the visible lines and a cursor on the active line.
Channel colors as semantics: function blue, type violet, macro orange, global green, constant yellow, external brown.
Instrument readouts in monospace with tabular numerals; prose in a humanist sans with Bulgarian Cyrillic support.
Motion explains: a pulse along the arrows, a capture flash where you land, a frame ping on the timeline. Nothing loops.

rules.name: The Resistor Code Rule
rules.body: Channel colors map to roles and never to decoration. A new role takes the next free channel, not a new hue.

rules.name: The One Pointer Rule
rules.body: Cursor yellow marks position only. It never decorates a surface or a label.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change on screen uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Hairline-or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface is defined either by its hairline or by a lift. Popups carry the hairline and a tight shadow, never a wide diffuse glow.

dos: Do bind every new color to a role in the channel table.
Do keep motion under 300ms, ease-out, on transform and opacity; the one exception is the stroke pulse on diagram edges.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion by dropping movement and keeping opacity changes.
Do keep numerals tabular and code on 13px mono.
donts: Don't add a decorative grid behind code; the graticule belongs to the diagram canvas and the timeline scale.
Don't use cursor yellow as a fill color for decoration.
Don't put a kicker above any heading.
Don't replace the SVG icon set with text glyphs.
